annotations.title: Make a set in another language

description: Use this when the user wants a screenshot set or listing asset in another language (a localization for the App Store or Google Play): one they saved (asset_id), or one you made in this conversation (handle). You translate every text layer yourself (get_asset lists them, with their ids); this makes a copy in that language, its images copied and the original untouched, wrapping a long translation and moving the captions under it down as the editor's own Translate set does. A saved set's copy is saved into the same project (asset_id back); a copy of yours is a new set with its own handle and link, which joins the original's project when the user saves them. Returns a preview of every screen (check the line breaks) and warnings; fix any line with edit_asset. One call per language. With asset_id (something the user saved) it needs the user signed in to appdesigns (in Claude Code type /mcp, pick appdesigns and choose Authenticate (or run `claude mcp login appdesigns` in a separate terminal), in Codex run `codex mcp login appdesigns`; other agents open the sign-in page themselves); with handle (a set or design you made in this conversation, not saved yet) it needs no sign-in.

handle.description: Instead of asset_id: the project_handle create_project returned or the design_handle create_design returned, for something you made in this conversation that the user has not saved yet. Needs no sign-in.

language.description: App Store Connect's code for the language, such as de-DE, fr-FR, ja, es-MX or pt-BR.

texts.description: Every text layer that has words, translated. Keep names and brands as written; match the source's tone and length where the language allows.

id.description: The text layer's id from get_asset.

text.description: The text in the new language; \n breaks a line.

name: translate_asset
title: Make a set in another language
